messages:
maya: heads up — support just escalated a customer report: embeddings endpoint returning 500s and 'dimension mismatch' errors when they send batched requests. High impact, customer in prod complaining about failed ranker.

eli: on it. which model and approx qps? any recent deploys? @akshay fyi since runtime batching touched last week.

maya: model is text-embedding-ada-002-like (1536 dims). They batch 8 inputs per request. QPS ~12 for that customer. We shipped a batching optimizer earlier today (deploy 1798009999) that changed how we validate shapes across shards.

akshay: got it. suspect batching validator change. Can we get a repro payload? maya, can you paste a minimal curl from the customer?

maya: pasted below (sanitized):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-ada-002-like","input":["short text","longer text here", "...", "...","...","...","...","..."]}'
```

support-bot: pd alert triggered: INCIDENT-1763 (embeddings partial degradation) — Severity: high — Affected customers: 1 (paying) — error rate spike 5x in past 12m.

eli: can reproduce locally with their payload. Getting a runtime error: `Batching error: inconsistent dims in batch (expected 1536, got 768)`. Logs attached from runtime: 

```
2026-03-15T10:12:01Z runtime[worker-3]: TRACE batch_coordinator: accepted batch of size 8
2026-03-15T10:12:01Z runtime[worker-3]: ERROR model_shard: embedding_vec_size_mismatch expected=1536 got=768 request_id=req_9b3
2026-03-15T10:12:01Z runtime[worker-3]: ERROR batching: aborting batch due to inconsistent output shapes
```

akshay: that log matches the validator logic change — we added a fast-path that skips per-request model selection when all requests claim same model name. If one item in a batch was routed to a quantized alias (768) and others to full (1536), the validator throws. Shouldn't happen because routing should normalize to canonical model.

eli: hypothesis — routing cache returning stale mapping for one traffic shard. I see a cache miss/backoff pattern in edge logs for ~10:12:00. Could be a race where the alias mapping updated during our deploy rollout.

samantha: customer says issue started at 10:11 UTC and intermittently affects ~30% of their batched requests. They turned batching off as workaround but want root cause and fix.

maya: customer workaround confirmed: single-item requests succeed. When they batch, roughly 1/3 fail with 500 + dimension message.

akshay: immediate mitigation: disable cross-shard fast-path in runtime via feature flag. I can flip ff.batch_fast_path=false for the fleet. It's a config toggle, no deploy. Will do in 2m if no objections.

eli: please proceed. Also scale up dedicated workers for embeddings to buy time if rollback introduces load.

akshay: flipping flag now...

deploy-bot: config-change: ff.batch_fast_path set to false by akshay (change-id cfg-2026-03-15-01). Rolling to 90% of nodes.

eli: monitoring... error rate dropping. current error rate from 32% -> 4% in 3m.

maya: customer confirms errors reduced, says still occasional failures (~1%) — probably tail effects. They're happy for now but want timeline for full fix.

akshay: next steps: revert the validator change in next patch, add stronger assertions for alias normalization, and add unit + integration test that simulates mixed-alias batches. I’ll open a PR and schedule a canary deploy after CI. Tentative ETA 6 hours.

eli: assign to eng-runtime priority P1. akshay, can you include the exact commit and the rollout window in the PR? Also add a runtime metric for 'batch_inconsistent_shapes' to alert earlier.

akshay: will do. Creating PR now. PR: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pulls/5123 — includes tests and metric emit. Marking for canary 11:00 UTC.

support-bot: updated INCIDENT-1763 status -> mitigated (partial): "batch_fast_path disabled, errors reduced. Root fix in progress".

eli: postmortem notes to collect: customer repro payload, edge routing cache timeline, deploy timeline for earlier change 1798009999, and why alias normalization failed. Also add guidance for customers to avoid mixed-model batching.

maya: filing support ticket with customer-facing summary and estimated fix time (6h). They'll get credit for downtime.

akshay: quick note on repro: I reproduced by forcing a cached alias mapping on one worker: `alias_map['text-embedding-ada-002-like-quant']=768` while others returned 1536. That triggers the exact error. Fix in PR ensures canonicalization before batch validation.

eli: good. Also experienced a small latency spike during rollback window — increasing worker warmup contributed. I'll monitor latencies; reach out if >10% p90.

samantha: looping in account exec @sarah to coordinate credits and comms.

maya: customer asked for a short postmortem. We'll share a redacted one after root cause confirmed.

akshay: pushing change to main after review. Will post deploy id and canary metrics to this thread once canary completes.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: runtime/main@sha256:9f7cc -> started at 11:02 UTC (canary 5%).

eli: canary metrics look good at 5%. Increasing to 25%. No spike in batch_inconsistent_shapes metric (0).

akshay: canary -> 100% complete at 11:28 UTC. Deploy id 1798127800. Closing incident when customer verifies.

maya: customer verified full fix at 11:40 UTC. All batched requests succeeded in their test window.

support-bot: INCIDENT-1763 status -> resolved. Root cause: routing alias cache inconsistency + new fast-path validation that assumed uniform canonicalization. Fix: revert fast-path, add canonicalization and tests, add metric and an alert.

eli: follow-up tasks — 1) postmortem doc in #postmortems with timeline and lessons, 2) add e2e test for mixed-alias batches in CI, 3) add warmup smoothing during config toggles. akshay/maya to own.

maya: will prepare customer-facing summary draft, share in 1h.

akshay: PR merged and deploy rolled. Will add the metric dashboard tile.

eli: thanks everyone. nice rapid response. :thumbsup:

maya: closing thread and moving postmortem tasks to tracker.
